html:
SMTO-EML-0030 — The mail server doesn't allow this sender's sign-in method

GUID: 23853c53-ade6-5e15-aab0-214642c50758
Slug: email-smtp-auth-mechanism-unavailable
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • The mail server doesn't offer, or doesn't permit, the sign-in method this sender uses. No email was sent, and this doesn't mean your password is wrong.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask your email administrator which sign-in methods the mail server allows for sending, and whether your mailbox may use them. The server either doesn't offer this method or its rules block it for your account.
  2. If the sender uses OAuth, open it in More options › Parameter Store (Value, then Reveal & edit value), set sasl_mechanism to xoauth2 or oauthbearer as advised, and select Save. SMTO only uses the sign-in method saved in the sender.
  3. If password sign-in is blocked, create a new sender from an OAuth Email / SMTP template, such as Microsoft 365 OAuth or Google Workspace OAuth. Some providers only allow approval-based (OAuth) sign-in for sending mail.
  4. Ask SMTO in a conversation to test the connection for the updated sender. The test confirms the server accepts the new sign-in method.

What success looks like

  • The connection test reports success.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details, which include the server's reply code, to your email administrator. Don't change your password; this error is about the sign-in method, not the password.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The configured SASL mechanism is not advertised in the server's EHLO AUTH capabilities, or SMTP AUTH returned 432 or 534 (password transition needed, or mechanism too weak or not permitted by policy).

What this means

  • The selected authentication mechanism is unavailable or does not meet the server policy. Classification uses the SMTP reply or negotiated capability, never the server response prose.

Why this can happen

  • The selected mechanism is absent from EHLO capabilities or AUTH returns 432/534.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained operation, condition and effect evidence before choosing a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Compare auth.sasl_mechanism (OAuth) or the password-login mechanism with the server's EHLO AUTH list and the mailbox's SMTP AUTH policy, and read smtp_response_code in the result. Select a supported mechanism, switch to the provider's OAuth profile template, or have the mail administrator enable the intended mechanism, then rerun email.test_connection.
  • Check the server-advertised authentication mechanisms and mailbox policy; select a supported mechanism or ask the mail administrator to enable the intended one.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first; existing effect evidence and replay checks still decide whether a new attempt is permitted.

How to verify the fix

  • The reported prerequisite is satisfied and a new authorized operation returns its actual result.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a write whose external effect is still unknown.

Technical notes

  • Diagnostic presentation does not start recovery or alter authorization.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
